 Judgment

The plaintiff Bank has filed present suit against defendants seeking recovery of Rs.7,63,660.40/-
with interest at the rate of 15.5% per annum from the date of suit till the date of realization.
2. The brief averments of plaint are that:

The plaintiff is a bank incorporated under the Indian Companies Act, 1913 having its Registered Head Office at No.112, JC Road, Bangalore District, Karnataka State and a Branch Office amongst others at Binnipet Branch, Bangalore District, Karnataka State Pin Code-560076.
The defendant approached the plaintiff bank for a loan of Rs.9,50,000/- for the purpose of business.

The plaintiff bank after following necessary formalities of preparing credit investigation report, pre-sanction unit visit report and simplified common Appraisal of Memorandum of MSME loan, sanctioned aforesaid loan of Rs.9,50,000/- to defendants under Loan A/c No.170005058882.

Defendants executed letter of undertaking, hypothecation agreement and other necessary loan documents by furnishing registration certificate, GST certificate, FSSAI certificate of their unit along with KYC documents in support of said loan.

Thereafter defendants failed to repay the loan, which constrained plaintiff to issue demand notice seeking repayment of entire loan amount of Rs.7,63,660.40 with floating interest prevailing at that time.
Despite service of notice, defendants neither cleared outstanding amount nor replied the above notice.
Thereafter plaintiff approached DLSA by filing PIM No.1297/2024 and received order dtd.11.09.2024.
Hence present suit and it is prayed to decree the same as prayed for.
3. Despite repeated issuance of summons, defendants could not be secured.
Thereafter despite issuance of summons by way of News Paper publication in Kannada Prabha Newspaper dtd.23.09.2025, defendants have remained absent and they have been placed exparte.

Non starter report issued by DLSA, Bengaluru Urban clearly shows that, despite institution of said mediation proceedings, defendants have remained absent on several dates and consequently the said proceedings are closed on 12.09.2024.
Further the suit is filed on 29.04.2025 and date of disbursement of loan is 23.06.2022.
On exempting the period of mediation from 31.05.2024 to 12.09.2024 under Sec.12A(3) of Commercial Courts Act, the suit appears to be within time.

11. The aforesaid oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW.1 clearly shows that defendants approached the plaintiff bank for aforesaid business loan agreeing to repay the said loan with above interest and subsequently defendants have committed default in repayment of said loan.
The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the plaintiff bank is sufficient to show that the defendants are liable to repay aforesaid loan amount to plaintiff bank with agreed interest.
12. Hence the oral and documentary evidence adduced by plaintiff bank has remained unchallenged.
Hence the aforesaid evidence has inspired the confidence of the court with regard to advancement of suit loan by plaintiff bank.
Hence plaintiff bank is definitely entitled for relief sought in the plaint.
Further plaintiff bank has claimed current and future interest at the rate of 15.5% per annum on aforesaid loan.
However admittedly the loan is borrowed for the purpose of petty business.
Looking to the nature of loan and facts and circumstances of the case, the aforesaid interest appears to be exorbitant.
However considering the business of defendants, they may be directed to repay the aforesaid loan due to plaintiff bank with simple interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
Hence suit deserves to be decreed in aforesaid terms.
Hence, Point No.1 answered Partly in the Affirmative.

13. POINT NO.2:- For the reasons stated and finding given on Point No.1, following is;
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is decreed in part with costs.

The Defendants are jointly and severally are liable to pay a sum of Rs.7,63,660.40/- to plaintiff bank with simple interest at the rate of 12% p.a. from the date of filing of the suit till its realization.
Draw decree accordingly.
